output.brief: The rejections were most likely caused by a wrong temperature setting, not by the fungicide, the growers, or the carrier. When the Tallis system was introduced, the mandarin product record was copied from an avocado record and set to 7.0°C instead of the cooperative's 4.0°C. Every rejected container was booked through Tallis at 7°C. Every container booked at 4°C passed, including the ones using the new fungicide. The controller logs show Meridane's units held the setpoint they were given, so a refrigeration-failure claim against Meridane is unsupported. Suspending Lower Serra growers and switching fungicide would not address the cause. My confidence is fairly high, though I did not check the pre-cooling logs or Lower Serra's share in accepted containers. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4.0°C now, before the queued container sails on 10 Oct. Check the at-sea container's setpoint and have Meridane reset it. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification. Hold the claim and payment decisions until this is confirmed.
